**None of the three schools offered a 100‑level anthropology (ANTH) course that was credited for at least 4 hours in the 2018‑19 academic year.**

- **University of Tennessee – Knoxville (UTK)**  
  – The 100‑level offerings were *ANTH 110 – Introduction to Biological Anthropology* (3 credit hours) and *ANTH 117 – Honors Introduction to Biological Anthropology* (3 credit hours).  
  – No 100‑level ANTH course at UTK was listed with 4 or more credit hours.

- **University of North Carolina – Chapel Hill (UNC‑CH)**  
  – The 100‑level courses were *ANTH 101 – General Anthropology* (3 credit hours) and *ANTH 104 – Introductory Biological Anthropology* (3 credit hours).  
  – UNC‑CH’s catalog values for 100‑level ANTH courses in 2018‑19 are all 3 credit hours; none reached 4 or more.

- **Missouri Southern State University (MSSU)**  
  – The 100‑level course was *ANTH 0101 – General Anthropology* (3 credit hours).  
  – MSSU did not list any 100‑level ANTH course of ≥4 credit hours in 2018‑19.

Because each university’s 100‑level ANTH courses in 2018‑19 were 3‑credit hours (and no repeatable‑credit calculations change that fact), there was **no single 100‑level ANTH course that met the ≥4‑credit‑hour requirement** among the three institutions.
